task: Fix the Firefox extension bug where searching a contenteditable field for a needle with leading/internal literal spaces (e.g. "   to a brief") fails to match, because Firefox substitutes U+00A0 (NBSP) for consecutive spaces as the user types into contenteditable, while textContent still reads back as space-looking characters. Make the compiled matcher's literal-space handling tolerant of whitespace variants in PLAIN and WHOLE-WORD modes, leave REGEX mode untouched (JS \s already covers U+00A0), and explicitly address the replace-time consequence of a matched NBSP being overwritten by a plain-space replacement string. Promote or remove test/probe-whitespace.spec.js. Keep all 75 existing Playwright tests and 8 existing Selenium tests passing.

phases.name: Red-baseline the whitespace regression tests
phases.description: Write Playwright regression tests that reproduce the bug at the matcher level using real keyboard-typed contenteditable input (not hand-authored HTML), pin regex-mode as unchanged, pin the replace-time NBSP-collapse consequence, document the whitespace-variant decision, and prove the new tests fail against the current (unfixed) content/find-replace.js.
acceptance_criteria: A new Playwright spec file (e.g. test/whitespace-matching.spec.js) exists containing at least these distinct test cases: (1) typing '   to a brief' via page.keyboard.type into an empty contenteditable div, then searching PLAIN mode for the literal string '   to a brief' (three leading ASCII U+0020 spaces), must find a match — this is the exact repro from the diagnosis and MUST currently fail against unmodified content/find-replace.js; (2) the same typed-NBSP scenario in WHOLE-WORD mode with a leading space in the needle; (3) a hand-authored (non-typed) contenteditable containing real ASCII spaces still matches the same needle (regression guard proving the matcher itself is not broken by the fix, mirrors the existing diagnosis finding); (4) a REGEX-mode test asserting the pattern `\\s+to a brief` already matches typed NBSP content on current unmodified code (pins that regex mode requires no change and must PASS before and after the fix, not just after)

The decision on which whitespace codepoints the PLAIN/WHOLE-WORD literal-space character class must match is written down explicitly, either as a code comment at the relevant constant/function in content/find-replace.js or as a dedicated section in README.md, and names at minimum U+0020 (space) and U+00A0 (NBSP) as required, with an explicit yes/no decision recorded for each of U+2007 (figure space), U+202F (narrow no-break space), and U+2009 (thin space) — not left implicit

For every whitespace codepoint the decision document marks 'included', a dedicated test case exists in the new spec file asserting a needle with a plain space matches page content containing that exact codepoint at that position (test asserts on the literal codepoint via String.fromCodePoint, not by eyeballing a copy-pasted character)

A test exists covering the replace-time NBSP-collapse consequence: matching text that contains U+00A0 in the DOM, replacing it with a replacement string containing plain U+0020 characters, then asserting what the resulting node's nodeValue/textContent actually contains (either 'the NBSPs are gone, replaced by the literal replacement characters' or an alternate documented behavior) — the assertion must reference specific codepoints, not just string equality, and the chosen behavior is stated in prose in the same file or README.md

Running `npx playwright test test/whitespace-matching.spec.js` against the current, unmodified content/find-replace.js produces at least one FAILURE in test case (1) (and (2) if wholeWord shares the same needle-compile path) — the failure output (test name + assertion diff) is captured and quoted in the phase's completion evidence, proving the test is not a vacuous pass-either-way test
test/probe-whitespace.spec.js is either deleted or its content is fully absorbed into the new spec file with no leftover duplicate probe file in test/

The pre-existing 75 Playwright tests (all files under test/*.spec.js other than the new whitespace spec and the now-removed probe) still pass unmodified, run via `npm test` or an equivalent scoped Playwright invocation, with no test weakened, skipped, or deleted to make this true

phases.name: Implement the whitespace-tolerant matcher fix
phases.description: Modify buildMatcher (and its literal-space compilation path) in content/find-replace.js so PLAIN and WHOLE-WORD mode needles treat each literal space as a character class covering the decided whitespace variants, without touching REGEX mode or normalising page content, then turn every phase-1 regression test green and keep the full existing suite green.
acceptance_criteria: content/find-replace.js's buildMatcher/escapeRegExp path compiles each literal ASCII space (U+0020) in a PLAIN- or WHOLE-WORD-mode needle into a character class matching, at minimum, U+0020 and U+00A0, plus exactly the additional codepoints marked 'included' in phase 1's decision document, and does not alter behavior when regex option is true

REGEX mode's source string is passed through unmodified by the fix — a diff of buildMatcher shows the `opts.regex` branch is untouched (no whitespace-class substitution applied to user-supplied regex source)

The page-facing DOM/value content is never rewritten or normalized by the fix — grep of the diff confirms no new writes to nodeValue/innerHTML/value in the matching (non-replace) code path; NBSPs already present in the page are left exactly as typed unless a match against them is actually replaced by the user's own replacement string
All test cases added in test/whitespace-matching.spec.js in phase 1 now pass, including the previously-failing typed-NBSP PLAIN-mode case and the whole-word case
The REGEX-mode pinning test from phase 1 still passes unchanged, demonstrating no behavioral change to regex mode

The replace-time NBSP-collapse consequence test from phase 1 passes and its asserted behavior matches the documented decision in README.md/CLAUDE.md — if the decision is that a plain-space replacement collapses NBSPs, README.md's Known limitations (or an equivalent documented section) states this explicitly as a conscious behavior, not left undocumented
The complete Playwright suite (previous 75 tests + the new whitespace spec, probe file removed) passes via `npm test`, with `test-results/gtest-results.xml` produced showing zero failures
The Selenium suite's 8 tests still pass via `npm run test:selenium`, unmodified and unweakened, confirming the fix does not depend on or break the real-extension activation/injection path

CHUNK_SIZE, the message-passing shape, and all other SPEC.md-mandated behaviors outside the matcher's literal-space compilation are unchanged (no incidental refactor beyond the matcher fix), verified by `git diff` scoped to content/find-replace.js showing only the buildMatcher/related-constant change plus any documentation touched
